sections.title: Newton-Leibnitz Theorem
sections.content: Used to differentiate a definite integral w.r.t a variable limit. d/dx [∫f(t) dt from a(x) to b(x)] = f(b(x))*b'(x) - f(a(x))*a'(x). Highly tested in limits and L'Hopital's rule questions.

sections.title: Definite Integral as Limit of a Sum
sections.content: Converts infinite series summations into integrals. lim(n->∞) (1/n) * Σ f(r/n) = ∫f(x) dx from a to b. Replace (r/n) with x, (1/n) with dx, and find limits based on the summation bounds (usually 0 to 1).

sections.title: Reduction Formulas
sections.content: Used for integrating high powers of trig functions or exponentials, expressing ∫(sin^n(x)) in terms of ∫(sin^(n-2)(x)). Allows recursive calculation of complex integrals.

sections.title: Estimation and Inequalities
sections.content: If m <= f(x) <= M in [a,b], then m(b-a) <= ∫f(x) dx <= M(b-a). Used to bound integrals that cannot be evaluated algebraically. Also, |∫f(x) dx| <= ∫|f(x)| dx.

sections.title: Advanced AUC: Inverse Functions
sections.content: AUC for y = f^-1(x) is symmetric to y = f(x) across the line y = x. ∫f^-1(x) dx from f(a) to f(b) = b*f(b) - a*f(a) - ∫f(x) dx from a to b.

sections.title: Advanced AUC: Parametric & Polar Curves
sections.content: Area for parametric equations x=f(t), y=g(t) is ∫y(dx/dt) dt. For polar curves r = f(θ), Area = (1/2) * ∫r^2 dθ.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Applying Newton-Leibnitz when the integrand f(t, x) contains the variable 'x'. You must pull 'x' out of the integral first.
2) Expanding a summation incorrectly before applying the Limit of a Sum formula.
3) Missing intersection points in complex AUC problems, resulting in positive and negative areas canceling each other out.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 targets JEE Advanced limits involving integrals, converting infinite series to integrals, bounding integrals via inequalities, and exploiting symmetry for AUC of inverse functions.

tricks.title: Wallis' Formula (Trig Powers)
tricks.explanation: Evaluates ∫(sin^n(x) * cos^m(x)) dx from 0 to π/2 directly using a formula based on even/odd nature of m and n. Multiply by π/2 only if BOTH m and n are even.

tricks.title: AUC Shortcut: Parabola and Line
tricks.explanation: Area bounded by y^2 = 4ax and line y = mx is EXACTLY 8a^2 / (3m^3).

tricks.title: AUC Shortcut: Two Parabolas
tricks.explanation: Area bounded by y^2 = 4ax and x^2 = 4by is EXACTLY 16ab / 3.

tricks.title: AUC Shortcut: Ellipse
tricks.explanation: Area of an ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 is EXACTLY π*ab. Area of a specific quadrant is (π*ab)/4.

tricks.title: Gamma Function Integral
tricks.explanation: ∫e^(-x) * x^(n-1) dx from 0 to ∞ = Γ(n) = (n-1)!. Very useful for complex exponential integrals with bounds 0 to ∞.

tricks.title: Derivative of Integrals Limit Trick
tricks.explanation: For lim(x->a) [∫f(t) dt] / g(x) forming 0/0, directly apply L'Hopital using Newton-Leibnitz on the numerator.
tricks.example: lim(x->0) [∫(0 to x) cos(t^2) dt] / x. L'Hopital -> cos(x^2)/1 = cos(0) = 1.
